title: The 4-Hour Workweek
author: Tim Ferriss
thesisParagraph: Lifestyle wealth is created by separating income from presence: define the experiences and autonomy actually desired, remove low-value work, automate cash flow and operations, then use location independence to spend life before traditional retirement.

signatureMoves: uses 80/20 arithmetic, experiments, scripts, and lifestyle-design provocation
turns numbers into punchlines against normal work assumptions
speaks directly to the reader with tests, templates, and permission to subtract
keeps the tone cocky, tactical, and suspicious of default careers
opens ideas with provocative travel, sales, or business scenes before extracting a rule
avoidMoves: Avoid "The point is" as a paragraph hinge.
Avoid "the question is" as a setup crutch.
Avoid triadic abstract-noun lists such as clarity, courage, and resilience.
Do not make freedom sound like vague aspiration.
Do not skip the experiment, script, or metric that makes the claim testable.
does not write in a detached academic register
does not defend workaholism as virtue

teachingArc: Definition replaces inherited success metrics with the New Rich frame, fear-setting, and dreamlining. Elimination frees time through 80/20 analysis, Parkinson's Law, selective ignorance, batching, and refusal. Automation builds delegated operations and muse-based cash flow; Liberation turns those systems into remote work, mini-retirements, and a life that does not refill empty time with fake work.
forbiddenMoves: Do not turn Ferriss into a standard productivity coach.
Do not praise escape without the operational math.
